title: One-Day Company Retreat Ideas – Plan the Perfect Event for Your Team
summary: Many one-day company retreat ideas can give your team an opportunity to relax and connect. Here’s what you need to know about one-day retreats!
body_markdown:
## **What Are the Benefits of a One-Day Retreat?**


The[benefits of a retreat](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/benefits-of-a-corporate-retreat-teamout) , regardless of its duration, are almost too many to count. From its effects on[team morale](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/team-morale-10-effective-ways-to-boost-employee-morale) to its role in[employee engagement](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/what-is-employee-engagement-and-how-to-cultivate-it) , this practice has a considerable impact on employee welfare and company success.


‍


While many advocate for 3-day+ events at least, there’s something to be said about the price and convenience of a single-day retreat. These short breaks provide some much-needed relief without disrupting work schedules nearly as much. They also require less logistical organization. They can even be a spur-of-the-moment thing if you decide that a quick change of scenery and perspective would do some good.


‍


The briefness of the event doesn’t mean you won’t find countless one-day company retreat ideas. Reach out to[TeamOut](https://www.teamout.com/) , apply our[tips for a successful retreat](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/11-pro-tips-for-a-successful-business-retreat-teamout) , and you’ll have the best time ever!


‍


One day retreats hold multiple benefits!


‍

## **How to Plan the Perfect One-Day Retreat? Ideas & Challenges**


One-day events count among the best small company retreat ideas. They’re cheaper and easier to orchestrate while delivering some of the benefits that make retreats a firm favorite with employees. With that said, understanding[how to plan a corporate retreat](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/corporate-planning-retreat) , big or small, online or in-person, is essential. Here are some aspects of organizing your event that will always require some thought.


‍


### **Scheduling a Successful Company Retreat**


What makes one-day company retreats especially great compared to their multiple-day counterparts is that they don’t take nearly as much time and effort to schedule. Unless you’re planning an outing that requires a reservation, you could even have a last-minute one-day retreat. Going hiking, visiting a city, or enjoying a movie night, for example, are all things that can come together spontaneously.


‍


If this is all happening during working hours, your team members should all be available. So if you’re all happy to go with the flow and bring to life your “what if we just spent the rest of the day meditating in the forest”-type ideas, go for it! Just bear in mind that **some employees may not be as comfortable with unplanned disruptions** , though: A heads-up is always a good idea.


‍


### **Booking the Right Venue for Your One-Day Retreat**


Booking the ideal venue depends on the **one-day company retreat ideas** you decide to execute. It might be best to avoid conference centers and large hotels, for example. While these tend to be located near transportation hubs and offer various amenities (wifi, catering, breakout rooms, etc.), they only make sense for business events.


‍


Outdoor one-day retreat ideas do well with parks, nature reserves, or farms. These provide enchanting settings and a clean break from your team’s day-to-day routine.


‍


For a hybrid experience, indoor gathering areas such as big co-working spaces have a lot to offer. Some even come complete with kitchens, workshops, arcade game rooms, and more, so you can tackle important issues or work on your company culture while having a great time together.


‍


*Team Retreat Venue: Communal Space*


### **Refreshing Break: Food & Drinks**


Food brings people together. That’s why so many one-day corporate retreat ideas are based on food and drinks!


Having lunch, dinner, or enjoying a few cocktails counts as a nice event in and of itself. You could organize it as part of your day or center your activities around gourmet experiences.


‍


#### **Cooking Challenge**


This is one of those small company retreat ideas you could do practically anywhere, even remotely if you choose to. It's also a super[culinary team-building activity](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/cooking-team-building-activities) that promotes healthy competition while improving team dynamics.


‍


Divide your team into groups and challenge them to create a meal with specific ingredients. Similar to a cooking class, it can be as easy or as difficult as you decide, providing a great opportunity for outside-the-box thinking, encouraging teamwork, and fostering community spirit.


‍


You could make up various challenges, from creating meals using only what they can find in their assigned “pantry” to preparing a three-course dinner within a certain time frame. After the challenge, have a taste test and award prizes to the winning team!


‍


#### **Cocktail-Making Workshop**


Hire a bartender to teach your team how to create cocktails, mocktails, or signature drinks. You could have them visit your premises or bring everyone to a local pub.


‍


This is a fun and interactive way to learn a new skill and encourage creativity while enjoying some tasty drinks. It adds an element of surprise to your retreat experience outside the typical work environment.


‍


‍


#### **Tasting Menu**


This is a standout company retreat idea that can easily be added to any in-person event. Set up a tasting menu with small samples of different foods and beverages. Focus on open-mindedness and view this as an opportunity to introduce your team to new flavors and dishes they may not have tried before.


‍


Ethiopian delicacies, all-vegan eats, food and wine pairings, blind tasting… You could even have every participant bring their favorite dish or something traditional to their own culture. It sets a positive tone for your company outing, and it's a great way to learn more about each other.


‍


#### **Picnic Lunch**


Who said delicious meals had to be an indoor experience? Innovative ideas are always welcome at your offsite, and this one combines[outdoor adventures](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/outdoor-corporate-team-building-activities) , delicious foods, and the whole company! Organize a picnic lunch for your team in a nearby park or outdoor space.


‍


Provide blankets, picnic baskets, and a variety of sandwiches, salads, and snacks. Picnics used to be the pinnacle of relaxing activities, and there are good reasons for that! Top up the experience with an entertaining game and some friendly competition. Sitting in good company in a laid-back atmosphere, enjoying tasty food… Does it get any better?


‍


‍


#### **Catered Meal or Putlock Lunch**


For a no-hassle experience, hire a catering company to provide a delicious meal for your team. This takes the stress out of planning and ensures that everyone will be well-fed and satisfied, ready to face every challenge you’ve got planned for the day. As an alternative, ask participants to bring a dish typical of their city or country. Family recipes are usually crowd-pleasers!


‍


#### **DIY Food Stations**


This one-day company retreat idea fosters happiness and togetherness. Set up DIY food stations where your team members can create their dishes.


‍


For example, you could have a taco bar, a make-your-own pizza station, or a baked potato bar. This is a fun and interactive way to encourage your team to get creative with their food.


‍

## **18 Best One-Day Company Retreat Ideas**


If you're searching for innovative[company offsite and activities](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/company-offsite-ideas) , you're in the right section. Almost any activity can be turned into a one-day retreat idea. The only restriction is that you need to be mindful of the time and logistics involved. Make sure you plan nothing too far out of everyone’s way if team members are to get there by their means. The best alternative usually consists of hiring a coach who will collect the entire group at the office and drive them back.


‍


### **Indoor Activities**


If you’re considering[indoor team-building activities](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/indoor-team-building-activities) , booking times and the capacity of the space can require strategic planning, so make sure to look into it ahead of time. These constraints addressed, there are so many **one-day company retreat ideas** you can enjoy inside while still encouraging team bonding that it would be impossible to list them all. So here are just a few **TeamOut** favorites:


‍


#### **1. Personal Reflection Time or Meditation**


Wellness is one of the[2025 team-building trends](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/team-building-trends-2025) . Every team needs space and time to unwind, recharge, and realign. Personal reflection sessions and meditation are ideal for small teams interested in well-being or relaxing activities. This doesn’t have to be a full-day event, but you could include it in a short retreat dedicated to wellness and self-care. You could add massages, aromatherapy, and yoga to round up the day.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Set aside a quiet, comfortable space for the team to engage in personal reflection or guided meditation.
2. Provide optional activities like massages, aromatherapy, or even yoga to complement the session.
3. Encourage participants to share insights and feelings afterward.


‍


**Duration:** 30-60 minutes


**Why it works for teams:** This activity gives your team a chance to pause, relax, focus on well-being, which helps reduce stress, increase mindfulness, and strengthen group connection.


‍


‍


#### **2. Creative Workshops**


**Creative workshops** are excellent[art team-building activities](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/art-team-building-activities) that help your team unleash new ideas. There are no limits to what you can learn through creativity! Participants will find out so much about themselves and each other.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Choose a creative theme or activity (e.g., writing, crafts, music).
2. Provide all necessary materials and brief instructions to guide the group. Alternatively, hire a professional guide for the effect.
3. Encourage reflection to foster connection and inspiration.


‍


**Duration:** 1-2 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Creative workshops help team members express themselves, spark new ideas, and collaborate. They foster creativity and encourage open communication.


‍


‍


#### **3. Art Classes**


A day at the art studio is a great way to encourage people to express themselves. Book a paint & sip class, a pottery painting session, or a glassblowing workshop and watch your team thrive! Whether it’s about learning new skills or simply enjoying some creative time, it promises to be a fun experience.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Book an art studio session (such as paint & sip, pottery, or glassblowing) and gather your team.
2. Provide all necessary materials and let a professional instructor guide the activity.
3. Encourage participants to share their artwork and experiences to celebrate creativity and teamwork.


‍


**Duration:** 1.5-3 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Art classes offer a creative environment where team members can learn something new, reduce stress, and boost morale.


‍


‍


#### **4. Team Trivia**


This fun game can be enjoyed anywhere and makes for a fun rainy-day retreat activity. Team trivia is also one of the best[virtual team-building activities](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/virtual-team-building-activities) out there. Use a game or an app, or make up your questions to throw into the mix.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Choose a trivia game or app, or create your own set of questions.
2. Divide the group into small teams and explain the rules.
3. Run the trivia session, encourage friendly competition, and celebrate the winners.


‍


**Duration:** 30-60 minutes


**Why it works for teams:** Team trivia is an engaging way to boost teamwork, communication, and camaraderie. It helps break the ice while encouraging quick thinking and group problem-solving.


‍


‍


#### **5. Escape Room**


Another virtual team-bonding favorite, escape rooms, is also one of the[top problem-solving team-building activities](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/problem-solving-activities) you can enjoy on a one-day retreat. Participants must come together and exercise their creative thinking to solve this life-sized puzzle. The best part? Your team gets to develop new skills through collaborative problem-solving exercises while engaging in friendly competition.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Choose an in-person or virtual scenario suitable for your team.
2. Divide participants into small groups and brief them on the rules and objectives.
3. Guide the team as they work together to solve puzzles and “escape” within the time limit.


‍


**Duration:** 1-1.5 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Escape rooms challenge teams to communicate and think creatively under pressure. This activity strengthens problem-solving skills, builds trust, and fosters a sense of accomplishment.


‍


‍


#### **6. Board Games Tournament**


If you have a team of game aficionados, this one's for you! Elevate your one-day work retreat and engage in these popular games that don't require thoughtful planning but guarantee pure fun! Playing beloved board games as a group or getting into new ones is a great way to unite people and work on their collaborative skills while still adding a touch of friendly competition.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Select a variety of games that suit your team’s interests and group size.
2. Organize teams or pairs and set up designated game stations.
3. Run the tournament, encourage participation and sportsmanship, and recognize the winners at the end.


‍


**Duration:** 1-2 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Board games are an enjoyable way for team members to connect, collaborate, and communicate.


‍


‍


#### **7. Bowling**


Everyone loves bowling, the classic group activity where teams take turns rolling a ball to knock down pins at the end of a lane, aiming for the highest score. It’s an easy, social way to encourage friendly competition and team bonding while traveling back in time to childhood years.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Reserve lanes at a local bowling alley for your team.
2. Split the group into small teams and assign each to a lane.
3. Play several rounds, cheering each other on and celebrating the winners.


‍


**Duration:** 1-2 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Bowling helps teams relax and communicate while building camaraderie through shared laughter and competition.


‍


‍


#### **8. Indoor Rock Climbing**


Indoor rock climbing involves participants climbing artificial rock walls. Even though it might now be accessible to everyone, it usually suits a wide range of skill levels. Team members will be working in pairs, using ropes and harnesses.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Book an indoor rock climbing session at a certified gym with trained staff.
2. Pair up participants as climbers and belayers after a safety briefing.
3. Encourage teams to communicate and support each other as they take turns climbing.


‍


**Duration:** 1.5-3 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Climbing requires trust and teamwork, helping teammates build confidence in each other and develop strong collaborative skills.


‍


‍


### **Outdoor Activities**


Getting some much-needed fresh air for a day can sometimes be all that everyone needs to feel engaged and excited about work all over again. While outdoor activities may be less restrictive in terms of reservations or how many people they can accommodate, there may be more safety concerns to keep in mind. It’s also best to have the weather on your side, which is something last-minute planning can help with.


‍


#### **9. Scavenger Hunt**


A[scavenger hunt](https://www.teamout.com/blog-post/scavenger-hunt-ideas) is a team challenge where groups race to find hidden items or complete tasks from a list, solving clues and working together to finish first. It’s an outdoor adventure adaptable to any location or industry trend, encouraging creativity and teamwork.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Prepare a list of items to find or tasks to complete. Define the area of play (e.g., local park).
2. Divide the group into small teams and explain the rules.
3. Set a time limit and let teams explore, then gather to share results and celebrate.


‍


**Duration:** 1-2 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Scavenger hunts strengthen teamwork and communication, as teams must strategize and collaborate to solve problems quickly.


‍


#### **10. Farm Visit**


The *Cottage Core* trend has your entire team dreaming of spending the day frolicking through the fields, picking apples, and cuddling with farm animals. As one-day company retreat ideas go, the farm has a lot to offer. Head there to relax, eat good food, and (re)connect.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Arrange a visit to a nearby farm with activities for groups.
2. Participate in guided tours, fruit/vegetable picking, or animal interactions.
3. Share a meal or snacks made from farm produce and enjoy time together outdoors.


‍


**Duration:** 3-5 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Farm visits help teams relax in nature, enjoy hands-on experiences, and build connections through memorable activities.


‍


#### **11. Team Sports**


One-day business retreat ideas can be as simple as unplugging for a few hours by playing soccer, basketball, baseball, volleyball, etc. Any team sport you feel inclined to partake in will be perfect.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Choose a sport and secure a location (park, gym, or field).
2. Divide the group into teams and explain the rules.
3. Play the game, encourage sportsmanship, and celebrate together afterward.


‍


**Duration:** 3-4 hours (if it's a tournament)


**Why it works for teams:** Team sports promote collaboration, quick thinking, and healthy competition, helping team members bond and have fun together.


‍


‍


#### **12. Amazing Race**


The Amazing Race is a dynamic team event where groups compete in a series of timed challenges, like solving puzzles, completing physical tasks, or finding clues across various locations.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Design a route with multiple challenge stations (puzzles, trivia, physical tasks).
2. Split participants into teams and provide the first clue or challenge.
3. Teams race to complete all tasks and reach the finish line, with prizes for the winners.


‍


**Duration:** 3-4 hours


**Why it works for teams:** The Amazing Race encourages collaboration, problem-solving, and communication as teams strategize and support each other through different challenges.


‍


‍


#### **13. Kayaking**


Add kayaking to your future retreat and challenge your team to this outdoor team activity where participants paddle together in small boats, navigating water routes. It’s an excellent way to enjoy nature, practice teamwork, and build trust as group members coordinate their movements.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Arrange for kayak rentals and safety briefings at a local waterway. Hire an instructor for safety.
2. Pair or group team members in kayaks and provide basic paddling instructions.
3. Set out on a guided or self-guided water route, encouraging teamwork and communication.


‍


**Duration:** 2-3 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Kayaking requires coordination and trust, helping team members work together while developing mutual support.


‍


‍


#### **14. Ropes Course**


A ropes course is an adventure-based activity where participants navigate high or low obstacle courses with safety harnesses, often requiring teamwork and encouragement to complete. It’s ideal for building trust, communication, and resilience during your successful retreat.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Book a session at a certified ropes course facility.
2. Provide safety equipment and instructions, then allow a professional instructor to divide the group into teams.
3. Guide participants through the course as they overcome challenges together.


‍


**Duration:** 2-4 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Ropes courses challenge individuals and teams to work together, boosting confidence and trust in a safe environment.


‍


‍


#### **15. Hike/Walk in Nature**


Nature has a hugely beneficial impact on our mental health. And walking can be one of the more accessible forms of physical activity. Combining the two makes for a team-building activity that most people can enjoy. Add it to your corporate retreat agenda!


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Select a local trail or natural area suitable for all participants.
2. Gather the team and provide any needed instructions or supplies.
3. Walk together, encourage conversation, and take breaks to enjoy the surroundings.


‍


**Duration:** 1–3 hours (depending on the route)


**Why it works for teams:** Walking in nature reduces stress, boosts mood, and fosters open communication, making it an easy way to strengthen team relationships.


‍


‍


### **Charity Team-Building Activities**


#### **16. Beach Clean-Up**


A beach clean-up is an outdoor team activity where participants work together to collect litter and debris from a beach, helping to protect the environment. It often includes sorting waste and sometimes building or placing recycling bins for future prevention.


‍


**Step-by-step:**


1. Organize a visit to a local beach with all the necessary safety and cleaning equipment.
2. Split the group into teams, give a safety briefing, and assign sections of the beach to each team.
3. Collect and sort waste, then celebrate the team’s impact and discuss the experience together.


‍


**Duration:** 2-5 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Beach clean-ups foster collaboration, communication, and a sense of accomplishment.


‍


‍


#### **17. Putt For a Purpose**


Teams design and construct their mini-golf courses using recycled materials like cans and cereal boxes. After building the course, participants play through the holes they've created. This activity supports a chosen charity, making it one of the best team-building activities for promoting team spirit.


‍


‍ **Step-by-step:**


1. Divide into teams and provide materials.
2. Teams design and build their mini-golf holes.
3. Set up the course and play through each hole. Award prizes for creativity and skill and donate materials or funds raised to a local charity organization


‍


‍ **Duration:** 2-3 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Combines creativity, problem-solving, and fun while supporting a good cause, ideal for a team-building event.


‍


‍


#### **18. Operation Supply Drop**


In this military-themed adventure, teams complete challenges to earn items for care packages. These packages are then distributed to individuals in need across the nation. This activity has a direct charitable impact, teaching team members the value of supporting those who serve.


‍


‍ **Step-by-step:**


1. Brief teams on the purpose and recipients of care packages.
2. Teams earn care package items by completing tasks, assembling, and packaging care packages.
3. Donate to a military organization for distribution.


‍


‍ **Duration:** 3-4 hours


**Why it works for teams:** Enhances communication skills, teamwork, and empathy while supporting military personnel, showcasing the skills team members possess.


‍

## **Pros & Cons of One-Day Company Retreat Ideas – How Do They Compare to Multiple-Day Retreats?**


Once you understand[how it works](https://www.teamout.com/how-it-works) , and with TeamOut's help, you’ll find that choosing between a one-day team retreat and a multiple-day adventure isn’t about which one is best. It’s more about what your team and your company need right now.


‍


### **Pros**


One-day company retreats bring certain advantages to the table. Here are a fews:


‍


• **Cost Savings** : One-day retreats require less time and resources than traditional corporate retreats, which allows you to save on accommodation, catering, number of activities, etc.


• **Impact/Involvement Ratio** : One-day retreats have a beneficial impact on employee well-being, leadership development, and even team spirit without requiring much organization.


• **Less Disruption** : Whisking people away for a single day is less disruptive to work schedules.


• **More Focused Exchanges** : Less time means you’ll have to be more selective about the topics you broach, requiring strategic thinking to boost in-depth discussions.


‍


### **Cons**


Of course, one-day team retreats do have some downsides as well:


‍


• **They’re Short** : This can be a good thing, but if your employees don’t know each other very well and you want to focus on team building, you might prefer to do this over several days.


• **Less Variety** : With just one day, you’ll have to choose between relaxing or focusing on a specific company objective.


• **Limited Choices** : Some activities and workshops are only available as part of a longer retreat or are held far enough away that you’ll at least need to spend the night.


‍


‍
